name: Barbell Hip Thrust
machineIdentification: A flat bench plus a loaded barbell, usually with a thick pad wrapped around the bar. Your upper back rests on the bench and the bar sits across your hips.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your upper back against the long edge of a bench.
Roll a padded barbell over your legs to sit in your hip crease.
Plant your feet flat, shins vertical at the top of the movement.
Drive your hips up until your body is flat from knees to shoulders.
Lower under control without resting the bar down.
keyCues: Tuck your chin and keep your ribs down.
Squeeze your glutes hard for a beat at the top.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back instead of extending the hips.
Setting the feet too far away, which recruits the hamstrings.
Cutting the range short and never reaching lockout.

name: Hip Thrust Machine
machineIdentification: A low seat with a back rest and a padded belt or lap bar across your hips, facing a foot platform. Newer gyms have these; look near the leg press.
instructions: Sit with your back against the pad and feet on the platform.
Pull the hip pad down across your hip crease.
Set your feet so your shins are vertical at lockout.
Drive your hips forward until fully extended.
Return under control without letting the stack rest.
keyCues: Keep your ribs down — extend the hips, not the spine.
Pause at full lockout each rep.
Push through your heels, not your toes.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back to fake more range.
Setting the pad on the stomach instead of the hips.
Bouncing off the bottom of each rep.

name: Smith Machine Hip Thrust
machineIdentification: The Smith machine with a bench set inside the rails, bar padded and set low over your hips. The fixed bar path makes setup much easier than a free barbell.
instructions: Set a bench inside the Smith rails, parallel to the bar.
Sit with your upper back on the bench, under the padded bar.
Unlock the bar and settle it into your hip crease.
Drive your hips up to full extension.
Lower under control and re-lock the bar at the end.
keyCues: Position the bench so the bar lands on your hips, not your stomach.
Keep shins vertical at the top.
Squeeze at lockout for one full second.
commonMistakes: Placing the bench too far forward or back.
Hyperextending the lower back at the top.
Forgetting to re-lock the bar before sliding out.

name: Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip width.
Set your heels about a hand's length from your glutes.
Drive your hips up until your body is flat from knees to shoulders.
Squeeze at the top, then lower under control.
keyCues: Squeeze your glutes to lift, not your lower back.
Keep your ribs down as you extend.
Hold the top for two seconds.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back at the top.
Pushing through the toes instead of the heels.
Feet too far away, turning it into a hamstring exercise.

name: Cable Glute Kickback
machineIdentification: A low cable pulley with an ankle strap attachment. You face the tower and drive one leg back against the cable.
instructions: Set a pulley at the bottom and fit the ankle strap.
Face the tower and hold the frame for balance.
Shift your weight onto the free leg.
Drive the strapped leg straight back, squeezing the glute.
Return under control, then switch legs.
keyCues: Keep your torso still — no rocking forward.
Squeeze at the end of the kick, then hold briefly.
Keep the working leg mostly straight.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back to swing the leg higher.
Rotating the hips open at the top.
Going heavy enough that momentum takes over.

name: Hip Abduction Machine
machineIdentification: A seat with two pads on the outsides of your knees that you push apart. Often paired back-to-back with the adduction machine, which works the opposite way.
instructions: Sit with your back against the pad and knees inside the pads.
Set the starting width so your knees begin close together.
Push your knees apart against the resistance.
Pause at the widest point.
Return slowly under control.
keyCues: Lean forward slightly to bias the upper glute.
Hold the open position for a beat.
Return slowly rather than letting it snap shut.
commonMistakes: Using the whole torso to rock the pads open.
Letting the stack slam closed on the return.
Very short reps with heavy weight.
